newsitem.title: UK: Bloomberg has big hopes for share dealing system.
newsitem.headline: Bloomberg has big hopes for share dealing system.

text.p: Privately-held U.S. financial information group Bloomberg LP aims to launch a screen-based share-dealing system worldwide to compete with Reuters Holdings Plc's Instinet, Bloomberg chief Mike Bloomberg said on Tuesday.
He told Reuters his new system, called Trade Book, was handling about two million shares a day in the United States, where it focuses on the Nasdaq exchange.
He said Trade Book was aimed at taking away business from Instinet, which contributed 135 million pounds ($219.1 million) to Reuters earnings in 1996.

Bloomberg said Trade Book, which was launched a couple of months ago, is dwarfed by Instinet and that he only reluctantly entered the business as it competes with some of his company's existing subscribers.

"We will do it everyplace. We do two million shares a day and Instinet does 200 million shares a day but you got to start someplace...I have very mixed emotions about it. I really wish we were not in the transactions business," he said.

"But I can't sit here and let Reuters have a business that makes an enormous amount of money for it...when that money is going into developing competitive products to us. We have got to be in that business and so we are,"
Bloomberg said that the company would be a serious competitor but that Instinet would be difficult to unseat.

"In all critical mass businesses, it is very difficult to move people off something that they are comfortable with. You have to have a very much better product, a lot of luck and even then it's not clear you can do it so we have our work cut out for us on that front," Bloomberg said.

He said his company dominated the market in debt execution and money-market instrument executions over electronic systems, but that it did not plan to compete with Reuters and others in foreign exchange transactions -- though he did not rule it out in the future.
"It is a less attractive business and we do have our hands full with the equity part...but if that business continues to grow and Reuters were to stay in it then we would certainly do it as well."
